spec_family.name: New Construction Ceiling Prime
spec_family.description: Single coat primer application for bare drywall ceilings in new construction. Seals porous drywall surface for finish coat adhesion. No edge work required — primer overlaps onto wall area, wall primer covers later. Companion to SF_DRYWALL_CEILINGS_NC_PAINT (finish coats). Includes conditional floor protection when finished floors are present.

includes: Single coat primer application (all quality tiers)
Ceiling drywall inspection and dust vacuum
Ceiling opening/fixture protection — includes open holes and installed cans/boxes (spray method)
Lightweight window/door masking — pin plastic to catch fallout (spray method)
Conditional floor protection — rosin paper on hard floors, canvas/plastic on carpet (when finished floors present)
excludes: Spot-priming of fasteners (NC fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant — RC-001)
Edge work at ceiling-wall boundary (walls not yet primed, primer overlaps onto wall area)
Sanding after prime coat (belongs to finish spec SF_DRYWALL_CEILINGS_NC_PAINT)
Spray-only application method (only roll and spray+backroll in scope)
Stain blocking (PVA and acrylic latex primers are sealers only, zero stain blocking — RC-002)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier governing inspection intensity and material grade. All tiers receive single primer coat. Application quality is universal — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any tier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT differences for primer: inspection thoroughness, material grade (PVA at QT2-3, acrylic latex at QT4, high-build at QT5), and final inspection scrutiny. Application quality is NOT tiered.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for ceiling primer
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray+backroll is NC production standard. Roll for smaller jobs. No spray-only option.

configuration_dimensions.description: Ceiling surface texture affecting coverage and application rate
configuration_dimensions.notes: Texture affects coverage rate, roller nap selection, and application speed.

paintable_items.name: Ceiling Field Primer Coat
paintable_items.notes: Primary paintable item — single coat primer on bare drywall ceiling

protection_items.name: Ceiling Opening/Fixture Protection
protection_items.counting_rules: Source from PaintScope PS_META.EA.ROOMS_TOTAL; heuristic: 6 recessed light locations + 2 ceiling electrical box locations per room
protection_items.notes: Stuff and tape ceiling openings — both installed cans/boxes AND open holes. Open holes must be sealed to prevent overspray entering ceiling cavity and blown insulation from coming through.

protection_items.name: Window Opening Lightweight Masking
protection_items.notes: Pin lightweight plastic over window openings to catch fallout. Not intricate masking. Typically first masking in NC production sequence.

protection_items.name: Door Opening Lightweight Masking
protection_items.notes: Pin lightweight plastic over door openings. Typically only exterior doors installed at this NC phase (sliders, front entry, back entry, garage entry).

protection_items.name: Floor Protection — Hard Floors (Rosin Paper)
protection_items.notes: Rosin paper taped down over finished hard floors (tile, hardwood, LVP). Full coverage, all seams taped.

protection_items.name: Floor Protection — Carpet
protection_items.notes: Canvas drop cloths or plastic sheeting over carpeted floors.

variants.notes: Economy spray+backroll prime. Single coat PVA primer. Quick inspection.
Standard spray+backroll prime. Single coat PVA primer. Thorough inspection.
Premium spray+backroll prime. Single coat acrylic latex primer. Detailed inspection with mil thickness verification.
Critical spray+backroll prime. Single coat high-build primer. Critical inspection with raking light. Surface must be ready for semi-gloss+ finish system.
Economy roll prime. Single coat PVA primer. No ceiling fixture protection needed (roll method, no overspray).
Standard roll prime. Single coat PVA primer.
Premium roll prime. Single coat acrylic latex primer.
Critical roll prime. Single coat high-build primer.

protection_zones_required.notes: Ceiling openings — both installed fixtures and open holes
Conditional — only when finished floors present. Rosin paper for hard, canvas/plastic for carpet.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: No edge tasks — ceiling primer overlaps onto wall area. Wall primer covers the overlap later.

valid_input_states.notes: NC ceiling prime operates on bare new drywall only

output_state.notes: Ceiling prime produces field-primed state ready for finish coat

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Full mask required for finished walls — solid tape line at wall-to-ceiling junction with draped plastic along wall. Rare in NC (ceilings primed before walls) but required for repaint scenarios.
Unfinished walls need no protection — ceiling primer overlap is acceptable

floor_type.notes: PROPOSED — not yet in Site_Condition_Vocabulary_Reference.md. NC may have finished floors (tile, hardwood, LVP, carpet) already installed. Determines whether floor protection is needed.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Ceiling prime is typically the FIRST paint operation in NC production sequence
sequencing_notes.edge_work: NONE REQUIRED — ceiling primer overlaps onto wall area. Wall primer covers the overlap.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Floor protection (if applicable) → Ceiling openings/fixtures → Window masking → Door masking → Apply primer → Cleanup
sequencing_notes.masking_persistence: Window/door masking and floor protection STAY IN PLACE for subsequent NC phases (wall prime, ceiling paint, etc.)
sequencing_notes.companion_spec: SF_DRYWALL_CEILINGS_NC_PAINT handles finish coats after this primer coat

research_corrections.summary: No spot-priming of fasteners in NC
PVA and acrylic latex primers have zero stain blocking
No dry time specifications in specs
